system_description.narrative_title: Iran-Middle East conflict fuels global energy shock and political fallout
system_description.narrative_summary: A widening conflict involving Iran (and Iran-linked actors) and regional rivals is disrupting shipping, strikes energy infrastructure, and driving sharp volatility and price rises across oil, diesel and gas markets while provoking diplomatic efforts and political maneuvers. Described as an open system: military actions, economic sanctions, shipping risks, market expectations, and domestic politics exchange energy, information, capital and legitimacy across borders, producing reinforcing feedbacks (higher prices → policy shifts → supply responses → new security risks) and spillovers into consumer prices and elections. Ongoing mediation, election outcomes and policy choices (e.g., US posture, refinery/storage deals) act as control inputs that can damp or amplify the system’s responses, making outcomes path-dependent and globally contagious.
system_description.scope: Interactions among Middle East military escalation (Iran, Israel, Houthis and regional proxies), international shipping and maritime chokepoints (Hormuz), global oil and gas supply chains (production, refining, storage, tanker movements), commodity markets and hedging, and near-term political actors and events (US and Israeli politics, mediation efforts) that drive price, supply and security outcomes.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical-economic system linking international security, energy markets, trade flows and macroeconomic stability
adjacent_subsystems: Global commodity and financial markets (trading, hedging, sovereign/state finance)
Maritime trade, insurance and logistics (tankers, chokepoints, ports)
Domestic politics and elections in key states (US, Israel, Europe)
Energy industry infrastructure and corporate strategy (refineries, storage, majors)

variables.name: Conflict intensity
variables.description: The aggregate scale and frequency of kinetic and hostile actions across the regional military theatre.

variables.name: Maritime transit risk
variables.description: The probability and expected severity of disruptions to shipping through major sea lanes and chokepoints.

variables.name: Production capacity utilization
variables.description: The proportion of total extractive energy production capacity that is operating and available for supply.

variables.name: Refining throughput rate
variables.description: The volume of crude converted into refined products per unit time across the refining system.

variables.name: Oil storage levels
variables.description: The aggregate stock of crude and refined products held in commercial and strategic storage facilities.

variables.name: Tanker availability
variables.description: The available fleet capacity and effective readiness of tankers for transporting hydrocarbon cargoes.

variables.name: Shipping insurance premiums
variables.description: The market cost level for war-risk and route-specific insurance applied to maritime energy shipments.

variables.name: Commodity price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price level for oil, gas and key petroleum products.

variables.name: Commodity price volatility
variables.description: The short- to medium-term variability and uncertainty in energy commodity prices.

variables.name: Supply disruption rate
variables.description: The rate at which physical disruptions (attacks, strikes, logistical interruptions) reduce or delay energy flows.

variables.name: Sanctions enforcement strength
variables.description: The intensity and effectiveness of trade and financial restrictions that constrain energy-related transactions and logistics.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement intensity
variables.description: The volume and closeness of mediation, negotiation and diplomatic activity aimed at de-escalation or crisis management.

variables.name: Governmental policy responsiveness
variables.description: The speed and scope with which policy actors can design and implement measures affecting energy, trade and security.

variables.name: Consumer energy demand level
variables.description: The aggregate level of end-user demand for fuels and gas across households, industry and transport.

variables.name: Energy hedging activity
variables.description: The flow of financial hedging transactions (futures, options, swaps) undertaken to manage energy price risk.

variables.name: Commodity market liquidity
variables.description: The depth and ease with which market participants can execute trades in energy derivatives and physical contracts without large price impact.

catalysts.title: Ongoing Houthi strikes on Gulf energy and shipping
catalysts.description: Continued Houthi strikes on ports, refineries and shipping lanes in Yemen/Gulf, producing repeated energy infrastructure and transit disruptions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Houthis strike Yemen's Aden airport'; 'Oil Prices Rise as Houthi Militants Target Saudi Energy'; 'Yemen's Houthis say they hit Saudi Ras Tanura.'

catalysts.title: Qatar-led mediation negotiations with Iran
catalysts.description: Qatari and regional mediation efforts to secure a deal to end/limit hostilities between Iran and adversaries continue and could de-escalate the crisis.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Qatari mediators present Iran with new deal to end the war'; 'Iran hosts regional powers for talks to prevent fresh escalation.'

catalysts.title: South Korea decision on Strait of Hormuz deployments
catalysts.description: Seoul's decision whether to deploy naval/air assets to protect its shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, potentially altering transit security dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Iran threatens South Korean shipping group over Hormuz transits'; 'South Korea says considering deployment options to Strait of Hormuz.'

catalysts.title: Israeli government formation and Iran‑strike decision
catalysts.description: Outcome of Israeli coalition formation and resultant policy toward Iran may trigger renewed strikes or restraint, affecting regional escalation.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Netanyahu made plans to restart Iran strikes earlier this month'; 'Israel vote leaves door open to Iran attack.'

catalysts.title: Extension of Russian diesel export ban/quotas
catalysts.description: Russia extending diesel export restrictions and quota system, tightening product availability in international markets and shipping flows.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Russia to extend diesel export ban, use quotas to fulfil US deal' (export restrictions tighten supply).

catalysts.title: Gulf oil majors expand overseas strategic storage
catalysts.description: Producers increase overseas crude storage capacity (e.g., caverns in Singapore), shifting where oil is held and smoothing supply shocks.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Gulf Oil Giants Work to Expand Overseas Storage'; 'Singapore to store Saudi Arabian oil in caverns.'

catalysts.title: QatarEnergy buys US and other LNG to hedge Hormuz risks
catalysts.description: Large-scale short‑term LNG purchases and portfolio rebalancing to mitigate potential Hormuz transit disruptions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'EXCLUSIVE: QatarEnergy buys US, other LNG to hedge future Hormuz disruptions.'

catalysts.title: EU energy ministers meet to discuss winter price measures
catalysts.description: Ministers convene to consider interventions (subsidies, caps, demand measures) in response to soaring fuel and gas prices before winter peak.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'EU energy ministers to discuss soaring fuel prices as winter looms.'

catalysts.title: Winter heating demand surge
catalysts.description: Seasonal increase in heating demand across Europe and North America raises gas and oil product consumption, stressing markets already affected by the war.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'European gas touches €100'; 'Heating your home with oil could cost $750 more this winter'; 'winter looms.'

catalysts.title: Energy executives pull out of Gulf conferences over security
catalysts.description: Cancellations and reduced industry presence at Gulf conferences reduce business‑diplomatic contact and slow coordination/investment decisions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Exxon, Chevron cancel executive trips to UAE's ADIPEC'; 'ExxonMobil boss pulls out of Gulf energy conference over security concerns.'
